claims.claim: **Most accidental paediatric ingestions are well below a toxic dose**, but ⚠️ **a handful of agents are dangerous after 1 or 2 dose units or a mouthful** and demand a cautious risk assessment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Admit for observation whenever a small child might have ingested one of these — any concern is enough.** **Discuss all cases** with a senior clinician, Poisons Information or a clinical toxicologist. PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calcium channel blockers:** bradycardia, hypotension, refractory shock — **toxicity may be delayed beyond 12 hours with sustained-release preparations.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine:** coma of rapid onset, seizures, cardiovascular collapse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Propranolol and sotalol** (tolerated worse than other beta blockers): seizures, coma, ventricular dysrhythmias, hypoglycaemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sulfonylureas: hypoglycaemia, which may be delayed 8 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Theophylline:** seizures, SVT. **Tricyclic antidepressants:** coma, seizures, hypotension, ventricular tachycardia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Amphetamines (ice, speed, ecstasy):** as for prescription amphetamines, plus **hyponatraemia with ecstasy.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **GHB:** rapid-onset respiratory depression and coma, recovering within a few hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Camphor:** rapid-onset coma, seizures, hypotension. **Hydrocarbons, solvents and eucalyptus oil:** rapid-onset coma, seizures and aspiration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lead foreign body such as a fishing sinker:** nausea, abdominal pain, **delayed encephalopathy**, seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Naphthalene moth balls:** methaemoglobinaemia, haemolysis. Today most moth balls use paradichlorbenzene, which is less toxic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Carbamate and organophosphate insecticides:** cholinergic syndrome, coma, seizures. ⚠️ **Paraquat herbicide:** oropharyngeal burns, multi-organ failure, pulmonary fibrosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23
